PC: Obtain labs: complete blood count (CBC), basic metabolic panel (BMP), creatinine kinase (CK), cultures, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) studies, serum/CSF baclofen levels
Initiate appropriate work-up and management of ITB withdrawal syndrome
Administer IV diazepam or administer high-dose enteral baclofen
Obtain abdominal Xray to see pump placement and tubing position
Obtain dedicated spiral CT study to evaluate baclofen pump catheter
If catheter integrity is disrupted, eventual surgical exploration and repair is warranted; contact neurosurgeon and treat patient with oral baclofen.
Plan initial management of baclofen withdrawal related to intrathecal baclofen pump malfunction
MK: Develop differential of   Increased spasticity and agitation
Consider recent spinal surgery as increasing risk of pump malfunction
Rule out medical causes:   Sepsis or infectious  Meningitis  Dysautonomia  Malignant hyperthermia  Neuroleptic malignant syndrome  Other withdrawal syndromes
Develop a differential for fever and agitation that incorporates device-related diagnoses
SBP: Notify primary service (i.e. the service that placed the pump-in this case, pediatric neurosurgery)
Contact the patient’s ITB pump specialist to interrogate the pump and check the reservoir
If the problem is unresolved, contact the manufacturer (Medtronic 1-800-328-0810).
Call a rapid response/ code blue
